Hi all — quick operational proposal to resolve the ambiguity; I put the formulas in the attached pricing workbook and a clean markup in proposed_exhibitC_markup.docx. Summary below so legal has concrete language to review: 

1) Definition: replace 'packaging anchor' with 'Billable Token Units (BTU)'. BTU = sum over invoice period of (model_tokens_generated * model_weight_factor) + (embedding_units * 0.25). This gives us a consistent token-first metric that is not tied to line-item SKUs.

2) SKU consolidation: allow a 90-calendar-day 'consolidation window' after the effective date of the new pack. During that window: 
   - Minimum commit and floor calculations will reference the greater of (a) historical aggregated BTU across the three legacy SKUs for the prior quarter, or (b) the actual BTU measured on the consolidated pack, whichever is higher, to avoid accidental down-crediting during transition.
   - If product migration is initiated by Orbit and results in lower BTU due to different usage patterns, Orbit can request a one-time recalibration (not to exceed 10% downward adjustment) supported by the migration plan and usage telemetry.

3) Soft cap/crediting: operationally we can convert the soft cap cash refund into an account credit applied to subsequent invoices. Proposed legal language: 
   "In lieu of a monetary refund, Customer shall receive a non-transferrable account credit equal to the shortfall amount, to be applied against future invoices within twelve (12) months following issuance. Unused credits shall expire after twelve (12) months."

4) Invoice mapping: invoices will include a new line item 'BTU-adjusted usage' with the BTU number and the per-BTU rate used for that billing period. This keeps auditability high and resolves ambiguity at reconciliation.

Next steps: Marissa/Laura — if legal is OK with the crediting language and the BTU definition, we can incorporate the two markups and send to Orbit procurement. Sam — if that works, please confirm SKU consolidation timeline and whether Orbit can share the migration plan (high-level) so we can lock the recalibration guardrail.

Karthik

Redwood Inference
